title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade/Rollback, and Customer Requirements
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

This document consolidates best practices, reference architectures, packaging guidance, day-2 operations, and upgrade/rollback procedures for Redwood Inference private deployments (VPC-hosted and on-prem). It is intended for SREs, platform engineers, solutions architects, and customer success engineers who plan, execute, and operate private installations.

Goals
- Provide repeatable, auditable deployment and operations steps.
- Capture minimum customer prerequisites and recommended sizing for production SLOs.
- Standardize upgrade and rollback procedures to minimize user-facing risk.
- Surface common failure modes and validated mitigations.

Scope
- VPC-hosted private control plane and worker pools (cloud customer-managed VPC).
- On-prem packaged deployment (air-gapped / private datacenter).
- Day-1 deployment and Day-2 operational runbooks.
- Upgrade, canary, and rollback playbooks.
- Customer requirements library and checklist.

Supported topologies
1) Small proof-of-concept (POC) - single-region, single GPU class, non-redundant control plane. Not recommended for production.
2) Production VPC (recommended) - Multi-AZ worker pools, HA control plane (3 control-plane replicas), private VPC peering for data plane, NAT for outbound updates optional.
3) On-prem enterprise - rack-level GPU clusters with dedicated management host, optional air-gap with file-based package distribution and an internal image registry.

Reference architectures (summary)
- VPC Production (recommended):
  - Control plane: 3x t3.medium-equivalent or k8s control-plane on customer-managed cluster with TLS, mTLS between services.
  - Workers: GPU nodepool with nvidia GPU drivers and NCCL; recommended instance types: p4d.24xlarge / A100 equivalents for high-throughput inference.
  - Networking: Private subnets for workers, public/control subnets with strict security groups. VPC endpoints for S3/STS where available.
  - Storage: ephemeral local NVMe for KV cache + networked object store for model artifacts (S3, MinIO).
  - Observability: host-level metrics via Prometheus, centralized logs to Syslog/ELK, and tracing via Jaeger/OTel.

- On-prem (air-gapped) reference:
  - Packaging: OCI images stored in an internal registry (Harbor), signed artifacts, and an offline bundle for initial install.
  - Hardware: minimum 3 management nodes (HA), 3 GPU worker nodes for basic redundancy, recommended 6+ worker nodes for production.
  - Networking: private VLANs for data plane, restricted management network for control plane.

On-prem packaging and distribution
- Deliverables for on-prem installs:
  - Signed OCI images (sha256 digests) and Helm charts.
  - Offline artifact tarball with model artifacts metadata (manifest.yml) and install scripts.
  - Installation appliance image (ISO) for fully air-gapped environments (optional).
- Packaging checklist:
  - All images must be reproducible and signed.
  - Helm charts templated with customer values.yaml and documented overrides.
  - Versioned manifests + migration scripts for DB schema upgrades.

Pre-deployment customer requirements (minimum)
- Network:
  - CIDR allocations for control plane and worker subnets.
  - Firewall rules allowing specific ports (listed below).
  - Outbound access to Redwood update endpoints (unless air-gapped).
- Identity & secrets:
  - Customer-managed KMS/HSM credentials provisioned or ability to use cedar-managed keys for POC.
  - Service accounts for control-plane components with least privilege.
- Hardware & quotas:
  - GPU type(s) and count. Minimums for production: 6x A100 (or equivalent) across 3 AZs/nodes.
  - Storage: 2TB NVMe local per worker for KV cache and temp.
- Compliance & access:
  - Designated customer admin contacts, RBAC mappings, and audit logging requirements.

Common ports and firewall rules (example)
- Control plane API: 8443 TCP (ingress from customer admin and control-plane components).
- Worker websocket/data channels: 9000-9100 TCP (ingress from control plane only).
- Prometheus metrics: 9090/9100 TCP (pull model from control plane/agents).
- Registry access (if external): 443 TCP to registry endpoints.

Day-1: Deployment checklist (VPC and On-prem)
- Validate prerequisites: kube version, docker/containerd, Nvidia drivers, kernel versions.
- Bootstrap control plane: apply TLS certs, verify mTLS, ensure control-plane HA.
- Install observability stack: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki/ELK, and Jaeger.
- Provision GPU nodepools and validate node labeling and taints.
- Deploy model artifact store and test model download + checksum verification.
- Run smoke test: 5 concurrent inference requests, verify latency and KV hit rates.
- Enable audit logging and snapshot baseline metrics for 24-72 hours.

Deployment steps (VPC - condensed)
1) Prepare AWS/GCP/Azure resources per reference IaC (terraform).
2) Provision customer VPC, subnets, routing tables, NAT/IGW as needed.
3) Deploy k8s cluster (EKS/GKE/AKS or self-managed) and apply cluster security policies.
4) Install control plane Helm chart with customer values: api.host, tls.cert, s3.endpoint, kms.config.
5) Create worker nodepool(s) with GPU capacity and attach IAM roles.
6) Deploy sample model and run verification harness (scripts provided in repo).

Day-2 operations (observability, scaling, incident response)
- Observability & alarms:
  - Recommended SLOs: 95th-percentile p99 response time < 250ms for short prompts, availability SLO 99.9% for Dedicated Private clusters.
  - Key alerts: control-plane crashlooping, model pull failures, GPU OOM rates > 1% per hour, KV cache miss spikes.
- Scaling policies:
  - Scale-up: automatic nodepool scale based on GPU utilization > 70% for 10 minutes.
  - Scale-down: aggressive cooldown of 15 minutes with safety window to avoid churn.
- Routine maintenance:
  - Weekly: manifest and Helm diff checks vs. running cluster.
  - Monthly: security patching of control plane nodes and registry verification.
- Incident triage summary (runbook excerpt):
  1. Detect: verify alert and gather snapshot (kubectl, logs, metrics).
  2. Contain: cordon impacted nodes, switch traffic to fallback model variant or region.
  3. Remediate: restart pods, scale workers, or roll back recent control-plane release.
  4. Recover: validate end-to-end inference and restore normal traffic routing.
  5. Postmortem: create incident write-up and link to regression tests.

Upgrade, canary, and rollback procedures
- Versioning model:
  - Releases are semantically versioned. Control-plane and worker images upgraded independently with compatibility matrix documented in release notes.
- Canary upgrade steps (recommended):
  1. Prepare new release Helm chart and image digests in a staging namespace.
  2. Smoke test in staging with synthetic traffic (latency, p95/p99, accuracy checks for known prompt sets).
  3. Deploy canary to 5% of control-plane traffic using traffic-splitter or alternate endpoint.
  4. Monitor for 30-60 minutes for errors, latency regressions, and metric anomalies.
  5. If stable, progress to 25% then 100% with monitoring windows.
- Rollback playbook (fast rollback):
  - Trigger conditions for immediate rollback: repeated 500 errors > 1% across 5 minutes OR latency regression p99 increased > 2x.
  - Rollback steps: revert Helm release to previous revision, scale down new workers, invalidate intermediate caches only if safe.
  - Post-rollback: run compatibility verifier and hold release until postmortem complete.

Customer requirements library (template entries)
- Template: name, category, rationale, minimal acceptance criteria, recommended config.
- Example entries (short):
  - "KMS integration": security, "Customer must provide KMS endpoint and key ARN", acceptance: "Control plane can successfully encrypt/decrypt test secrets", recommended: "Use customer KMS with key rotation enabled".
  - "Model artifact storage": infra, "Customer provides S3/MinIO endpoint or accepts Redwood-managed storage", acceptance: "Model manifest fetch and checksum passes", recommended: "S3 with versioning and lifecycle rules".
  - "Network egress policy": security, "Restrict control-plane egress except update endpoints", acceptance: "Access to telemetry endpoints confirmed during install", recommended: "Allowlist minimal endpoints documented in appendix".

Ownership and contacts
- Primary owners: eng-private-deployments team (oncall rotation).
- Escalation path: oncall -> eng-platform -> eng-sre -> security if required.
- Support: customer-success for runbooks and schedule for kickoff.

Appendices
A) Example values.yaml (excerpt)
----
replicaCount: 3
api:
  host: "api.redwood.local"
  tls: true
storage:
  s3Endpoint: "https://minio.internal.local"
  bucket: "redwood-models"
kms:
  provider: "aws"
  keyArn: "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789:key/abcd-ef01"
nodePools:
  - name: gpu-pool
    instanceType: "p4d.24xlarge"
    min: 3
    max: 12
----

B) Sample verification commands
- kubectl -n redwood get pods
- kubectl logs deployment/redwood-control-plane
- ./tools/smoke_test.sh --endpoint https://api.redwood.local --requests 100

C) Troubleshooting quick references
- GPU driver mismatch: check nvidia-smi and kernel messages; reinstall driver package pinned to supported version.
- Model pull failures: verify registry credentials, bucket policies, and checksum mismatch in manifest.yml.
